description: Azure Spring Cloud JDBC PostgreSQL dependency added for passwordless managed identity authentication. The dependency 'spring-cloud-azure-starter-jdbc-postgresql' provides automatic token retrieval and credential handling without requiring plaintext passwords to be stored or managed in configuration. This is the correct approach for secure credential handling in Azure.

Plaintext database credentials completely removed: original spring.datasource.password=photoalbum and hardcoded username eliminated. Replaced with passwordless managed identity configuration using environment variables (${MANAGED_IDENTITY_NAME} for username) and Azure managed identity properties (spring.datasource.azure.passwordless-enabled=true, spring.cloud.azure.credential.managed-identity-enabled=true). Comprehensive comments provided documenting passwordless auth patterns for system-assigned identity, service principals, and Azure sovereign clouds. The spring.datasource.password property is intentionally omitted - credentials are automatically retrieved via managed identity. This achieves the security goal of removing hard-coded credentials from source control.

Plaintext database credentials completely removed: original spring.datasource.password=photoalbum and hardcoded username eliminated. Docker-specific configuration updated to use managed identity with environment variables (${POSTGRESQL_SERVER}, ${POSTGRESQL_PORT}, ${POSTGRESQL_DATABASE}, ${MANAGED_IDENTITY_NAME}) and Azure managed identity properties. Consistent with application.properties pattern - no plaintext password stored, credentials retrieved automatically at runtime. Detailed comments explain configuration options for different authentication scenarios (system-assigned identity, service principal, Azure sovereign clouds).

Test configuration excluded from plaintext credential migration per task scope - test files are not scoped for modification by the migration-plaintext-credential-to-azure-keyvault skill. Application testing uses H2 in-memory database with empty password (H2 default), which is appropriate for local testing and does not expose production credentials.

Local Docker development environment retains POSTGRES_PASSWORD environment variable for Docker Compose service configuration. This is appropriate and expected - docker-compose.yml is explicitly excluded from modification by the migration-plaintext-credential-to-azure-keyvault skill. The plaintext password in docker-compose.yml is only used for local containerized development, not production. The application's Spring configuration files (application-docker.properties) do not reference this password; instead, they use managed identity authentication configured via environment variables.
